issues.legal_issue: Long public use and the physical features and maintenance of a way may establish that adjoining side strips form part of the public highway.
material_facts: The landowner’s plot contained a metalled road, open strips on either side of it, and drains beyond the strips.
The public had used the road for decades, and the municipality had maintained the road and drains.
The open strips lay between the metalled road and the drains maintained by the municipality.
issues.conclusion: The side strips, including the disputed site, formed part of the public pathway dedicated to public use.
issues.legal_principle: Dedication of a highway may be inferred from long public use, and its width depends on the extent of that use. Side lands are ordinarily included where they are needed for the proper maintenance of the road; topographical features and the manner of maintenance help establish the extent of the public way. The Court relied on Halsbury’s Laws of England, 3rd ed., vol. 19, pp. 49 and 55; Harvey v. Truro Rural District Council; Rex v. Wright; Anukul Chandra v. Dacca District Board; and Municipal Board of Agra v. Sudarshan Das Shastri.

predicates.public_pathway_dispute: The proceeding concerns whether land adjoining a road is part of a public pathway.
predicates.long_public_use: The public has used the road for a long period.
predicates.municipal_maintenance_of_road_and_bounda: The municipality has maintained the road and the features marking its boundaries.
predicates.side_strips_between_road_and_maintained_: The disputed side strips lie between the road and boundaries or features maintained by the municipality.
predicates.side_strips_inferred_to_form_part_of_pub: The side strips are treated as part of the public pathway.

issues.definition: When a public-pathway dispute involves long public use, municipal maintenance, and side strips between the road and maintained boundaries, the side strips are treated as part of the public pathway.

issues.legal_issue: A municipality controlling a public pathway may not erect structures on it that are unnecessary for maintaining or using it as a pathway, and the soil owner may obtain an injunction against such structures.
material_facts: The disputed site was part of the public pathway, which vested in the municipality for management and control.
The landowner owned the soil beneath the pathway, subject to the public’s passage rights and the municipality’s rights over the pathway.
The municipality proposed to erect a statue and rooms for a drinking-water facility and a library on the site.
Those structures were not necessary for maintaining or using the way as a public pathway.
issues.conclusion: The proposed structures were unauthorized, and the landowner was entitled to a permanent injunction restraining their construction.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 116(g) of the U.P. Municipalities Act, 1916, public streets and specified things appertaining to them vest in the municipal board. Such vesting does not transfer ownership of the soil: it gives the municipality control of the surface and only so much of the space above and below it as is necessary to maintain the street. The municipality cannot use that control to erect structures unrelated to maintaining or using the pathway. The Court relied on S. Sundaram Ayyar v. Municipal Council of Madura and the Secretary of State for India in Council, and on the principle that the soil owner may protect their rights against acts exceeding the public and municipal rights over a highway.

rule.if: public_pathway_dispute and public_pathway_vests_in_municipality and soil_owner_seeks_injunction and proposed_structures_not_needed_for_pathway_maintenance_or_use

predicates.public_pathway_dispute: The proceeding concerns a municipality’s proposed use of land forming part of a public pathway.
predicates.public_pathway_vests_in_municipality: The pathway is subject to the municipality’s management and control.
predicates.soil_owner_seeks_injunction: The owner of the soil seeks an injunction against the proposed construction.
predicates.proposed_structures_not_needed_for_pathw: The municipality proposes structures that are not needed to maintain or use the land as a pathway.
predicates.soil_owner_entitled_to_injunction_agains: The soil owner is entitled to an injunction against structures unrelated to maintaining or using the pathway.

issues.definition: When a municipality controls a public pathway, the soil owner seeks an injunction, and the proposed structures are unnecessary for the pathway, the soil owner is entitled to an injunction against them.

issues.legal_issue: An owner of the soil beneath a public pathway cannot recover possession of land that remains subject to the public pathway and municipal control.
material_facts: The landowner owned the soil beneath the disputed site, but the site formed part of the public pathway.
The pathway continued to vest in the municipality for its management and control, subject to the public’s rights of passage.
The landowner’s suit sought delivery of possession of the disputed site as well as an injunction.
issues.conclusion: The landowner could not obtain possession of any part of the public pathway, and the claim for possession was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Municipal vesting of a public street under section 116(g) of the U.P. Municipalities Act, 1916, does not transfer ownership of the soil, but the municipality has control of the pathway to the extent necessary for its maintenance, while the public retains passage rights. The soil owner remains subject to those rights and cannot recover possession of a part of the public pathway. The Court relied on S. Sundaram Ayyar v. Municipal Council of Madura and the Secretary of State for India in Council, and the statement of the highway principle in Pratt and Mackenzie’s Law of Highways.

rule.if: public_pathway_dispute and owner_claims_possession and claimant_owns_underlying_soil and site_remains_part_of_public_pathway_vested_in_municipality

predicates.public_pathway_dispute: The proceeding concerns a claim to land forming part of a public pathway.
predicates.owner_claims_possession: The claimant seeks delivery of possession of the disputed land.
predicates.claimant_owns_underlying_soil: The claimant owns the soil beneath the disputed land.
predicates.site_remains_part_of_public_pathway_vest: The disputed site remains part of a public pathway subject to municipal management and control.
predicates.owner_not_entitled_to_possession_of_publ: The owner is not entitled to recover possession of the part of the land that remains a public pathway.

issues.definition: When an owner seeks possession of underlying soil that remains part of a public pathway subject to municipal control, the owner cannot recover possession of that pathway.
